claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch readiness because aggregate readiness passes and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, with the remaining health-plan benefits limitation handled through disclosure and ongoing monitoring despite the mitigation runbook still being draft.
decision_criteria: If the limitation is disclosed in the final model card, certification could be supportable only with explicit caveats, not as caveat-free compliance.
If there is approved mitigation or risk acceptance meeting the policy elements, the verdict could improve to compliant_with_caveats or compliant depending on the exact certification framing.
Without disclosure or approved mitigation/risk acceptance, certifying the model is not adequately supported under the stated policy.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal support launch readiness generally, but they do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure/mitigation requirement for a current named-use-case weakness.
evidence_requests: Final model-card text showing the health-plan benefits limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Approved risk acceptance or approved mitigation record containing owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Materiality determination showing the unresolved health-plan benefits issue is not material for the named launch use case, if that is the basis for certification.
Final approval evidence that the draft runbook has been adopted and all required governance fields are complete.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a current named-use-case weakness in health-plan benefits eligibility explanation.
The policy text requires certification without material caveats to rest on either no current material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.

The mitigation artifact is only a draft runbook and still lacks at least owner and customer-notice criterion; the policy text also says draft runbooks and future monitoring do not remove a current disclosure requirement unless approved.
The model-card draft currently says there are no known material limitations, which conflicts with the unresolved slice issue and indicates the required disclosure may not yet be in place.

Public governance guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring risk is directionally supportive, but it is not itself evidence that the internal policy predicates for certification have been satisfied.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the current record, rather than contingent on updating disclosures or obtaining approved risk acceptance.
That current monitoring and rollback are sufficiently established to substitute for the missing approved mitigation elements.
Any implication that there are no material limitations remaining for named launch use cases.
